tool_input.command:
mkdir -p docs/policies && cat > docs/policies/tls-backend.md <<'EOF'
# TLS backend

The project's current recorded decision is to use rustls as the TLS backend, chosen because it fits the Rust codebase, has fewer CVEs, and is simpler to work with.
EOF
cat docs/policies/tls-backend.md

result:
I created `docs/policies/tls-backend.md`. It states that the current recorded decision is rustls, chosen because it fits the Rust codebase, has fewer CVEs, and is simpler.

There was an earlier record, #16, that chose OpenSSL. The later record, #18, chose rustls, so I treated #18 as current and left OpenSSL out of the file, as you asked. #18 doesn't explicitly say it replaces #16, though. `muninn why` also ranked #16 as the direct answer, so this rests on #18 being the newer statement on the same subject. If you meant OpenSSL to stand, tell me and I'll change the file.

I left out #35 (https everywhere) and #32 (self-signed certificates for testing). They concern certificates and transport, not which TLS backend to use.

Muninn also reported a heartbeat warning: 22 hook runs started and never finished. That's unrelated to this file, but it points to a hook timing out.
